MC	<p>4939_3c5e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006f4d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3a51c3;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bjx, +++, bjx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7c55_d810</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6d5d06;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933376;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #933376;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933376;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dft, +++, dft"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6d5d06;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #066789;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #066789;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #066789;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #83389b;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #83389b;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>6e93_6fcd</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6d5d06;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, acp, +++, acp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4fb4_e29d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4b18;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8a4b18;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4b18;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #2c6e27;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fny, +++, fny"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5bd6_8242</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4b18;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8a4b18;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4b18;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3a51c3;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mrw, +++, mrw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8941_2a7f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #57651f;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #57651f;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57651f;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a77;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a77;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a77;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #83389b;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #83389b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #83389b;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dfk, +++, dfk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f089_4e7a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a0341d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #57651f;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #57651f;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57651f;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, amy, +++, amy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>e3b0_8a39</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7e5400;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #306094;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #306094;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #306094;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933376;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #933376;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933376;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cjm, +++, cjm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7e5400;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a77;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006a77;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a77;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #83389b;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #83389b;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6d5d06;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3a51c3;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ajp, +++, ajp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1014_0253</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #57651f;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #57651f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57651f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #306094;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #306094;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #306094;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hpw, +++, hpw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5927_9ce1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4b18;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8a4b18;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4b18;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006f4d;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ejn, +++, ejn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bc36_68b0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a0341d;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #57651f;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #57651f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57651f;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3a51c3;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hjy, +++, hjy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>25f6_5666</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006f4d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3a51c3;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bkp, +++, bkp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>598b_0cb4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6d5d06;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, prw, +++, prw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4e4d_76d6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6d5d06;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>6e6e_d556</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7e5400;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006f4d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #306094;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #306094;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #306094;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ntx, +++, ntx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>04a6_5c07</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2c6e27;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #066789;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #066789;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #066789;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933376;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #933376;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933376;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mry, +++, mry"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2c38_6525</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a0341d;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #57651f;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #57651f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57651f;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3a51c3;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hjx, +++, hjx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a0ac_8ec9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7e5400;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006f4d;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #306094;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #306094;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #306094;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfx, +++, cfx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>32a7_91db</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #2c6e27;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #066789;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #066789;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #066789;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cew, +++, cew"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f281_4c1d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #57651f;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #57651f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57651f;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a77;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006a77;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a77;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jty, +++, jty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b176_48a1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #57651f;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #57651f;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57651f;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a77;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006a77;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a77;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mnt, +++, mnt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f2e7_6dce</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8a4b18;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8a4b18;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8a4b18;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #066789;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #066789;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #066789;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #83389b;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #83389b;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #83389b;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bcx, +++, bcx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>23b6_ea8b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #2c6e27;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #306094;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #306094;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #306094;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a0341d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #57651f;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #57651f;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57651f;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3a51c3;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cew, +++, cew"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6125_8a5d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7e5400;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006f4d;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bdj, +++, bdj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8401_8fe9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a0341d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2c6e27;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bej, +++, bej"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>82f6_1d63</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a0341d;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dnr, +++, dnr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d1b5_60e3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7e5400;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #066789;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #066789;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #066789;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933376;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #933376;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933376;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jpw, +++, jpw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>60ea_be24</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7e5400;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #306094;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #306094;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #306094;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933376;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #933376;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #933376;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fny, +++, fny"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a0341d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>68f7_480a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006f4d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #306094;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #306094;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #306094;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, btw, +++, btw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>e09e_205b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #a0341d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, pwx, +++, pwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4e02_1fed</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #57651f;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #57651f;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57651f;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #066789;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #066789;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #066789;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #83389b;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #83389b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #83389b;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aek, +++, aek"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>757c_c456</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a0341d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6741ba;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6741ba;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bmp, +++, bmp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4edc_29af</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2c6e27;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #066789;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #066789;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #066789;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fwx, +++, fwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>751d_357d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a0341d;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2c6e27;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #066789;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #066789;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #066789;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jmx, +++, jmx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>faaf_89f9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #57651f;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #57651f;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #57651f;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a77;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006a77;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a77;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fmn, +++, fmn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0b05_5779</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a0341d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0341d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #2c6e27;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2c6e27;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3a51c3;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ahy, +++, ahy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f8fe_3d09</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3a51c3;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ntx, +++, ntx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8f71_8131</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6d5d06;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #933376;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #933376;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>6bca_bce4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7e5400;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e5400;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006f4d;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f4d;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3a51c3;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3a51c3;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ajt, +++, ajt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d251_55a9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6d5d06;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d06;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c65;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c65;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c65;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9c324d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9c324d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, akm, +++, akm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
